https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.title: UA.Negotiations Update May.21.2026
https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: (847) 640-2222 @) IAM141.org United Airlines Negotiations Update May 21, 2026 IAM Members at United Airlines , IAM District 141 is pleased to announce that Agreements in Principle have been reached through the collective bargaining process.; After months of determined negotiations and the unwavering solidarity of our membership, we have achieved a historic milestone.; This proposed five-year agreement delivers meaningful gains and industry-leading improvements, including: • Industry-leading wage rates across every contract • 1-step reduction of wage scale progressions • Expansion of Observed Holidays from 6 to 10 • System-wide layoff protections for all employees on the payroll as of the Date of Ratification • Improved vacation accrual and enhanced retirement benefits throughout the life of the agreement • Paid maternity and parental leave • Stronger grievance procedure protections • An end to the unlimited use of relief lines • A signing bonu s • Numerous additional contractual improvements that will directly benefit our members and their families Complete details outlining all negotiated changes will be made available to the membership no later than Tuesday, May 26, 2026.; The District 141 United Airlines Negotiations Committee is currently finalizing the language and preparing the ratification process and schedule.; I also want to recognize and thank the District 141 Negotiations Committee for their tireless work and steadfast commitment to protecting our membership's interests.; Additionally, I extend my appreciation to Air Transport General Vice President Richie Johnsen and his staff for their continued guidance and support throughout negotiations.; IAM District 141 Negotiating Team Olu Ajetomobi Joe Bartz Jill Hazamy Victor Hernandez Barb MartinMichael G.

https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/arizona.text: 6, 2026 — IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers) Local 933 members have opened contract negotiations with Raytheon in Tucson, Ariz., calling for an agreement that recognizes their highly skilled work and critical role in protecting national security.; We stand firmly with Local 933 members as they work to secure the wages, benefits and security they have earned.” The opening of negotiations follows months of preparation and member engagement.; Members carried that unity into multiple solidarity rallies ahead of negotiations, sending a clear message to Raytheon management and the Tucson community: the workers behind these vital defense systems are standing together for a strong contract.; See photos: IAM Local 933 Members Rally Ahead of Contract Negotiations with Raytheon “Local 933 members have made their priorities clear, and they have backed them up by standing shoulder to shoulder,” said IAM Western Territory General Vice President Robert “Bobby” Martinez.; The company needs to come to the table ready to negotiate an agreement that reflects those contributions and improves the lives of these workers and their families.” Earlier this year, the Local 933 bargaining committee completed intensive Negotiation Prep training at the William W.; The committee is also receiving support from the IAM International Union and the IAM Western Territory throughout negotiations.; The turnout at our union meetings, town halls, and rallies shows we are united and ready to fight for the contract we deserve.”

https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/iam-uni.title: IAM Union NASSCO Shipbuilders Ratify Groundbreaking New Contract with Nearly 20% Wage Increases and Major Benefit Gains
https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/iam-uni.text: 17, 2026 — IAM Union members at General Dynamics NASSCO have ratified a strong new three-year collective bargaining agreement covering more than 800 shipbuilders in San Diego with massive wage and benefit gains.; “Our members stood together throughout this campaign, and their solidarity produced meaningful improvements in wages, retirement security, benefits and workplace protections.” The ratification followed a months-long internal organizing and mobilization campaign led by IAM Local 389 and IAM District 947.; During the campaign, membership within the NASSCO bargaining unit grew from approximately 21% to more than 67%, significantly strengthening workers’ collective voice at the negotiating table.; IAM Western Territory Special Representative Luis Silvas served as the negotiating committee’s spokesperson throughout bargaining.; This contract shows what solidarity can achieve, and we will keep building that strength to win even more for NASSCO shipbuilders in the future.” “This outcome belongs to the members who organized, attended meetings, participated in workplace actions, and supported their negotiating committee every step of the way,” said IAM District 947 President and Directing Business Representative Sal Vasquez.; “They proved that when workers become members, get involved, and remain united, they can win a contract that moves everyone forward.” IAM District 947 Business Representative William “Billy” Corona helped lead the internal organizing campaign and supported the committee throughout negotiations.; That unity gave the committee the power it needed to secure real gains at the table.” The IAM negotiating committee included NASSCO shipbuilders and IAM members Adrian Contreras, Stanley Huddleston, and Armando Ybhoa, who brought their coworkers’ priorities and experiences directly to the bargaining table.; The negotiating team also received support from IAM District 947 Organizer Alberto Delfin, who played a key role in the internal organizing and mobilization efforts that strengthened member participation and solidarity throughout the campaign.; “We are proud of what NASSCO shipbuilders accomplished together,” said the Negotiating Committee.; “Our members made their priorities clear, stood behind their committee, and stood in solidarity throughout negotiations.; The ratified agreement reflects the growing strength and solidarity of IAM Local 389 members and their commitment to building a stronger future for every NASSCO shipbuilder.

https://www.goiam.org/news/iam-local-62a.title: IAM Local 62A Opens Contract Negotiations with Collins Aerospace
https://www.goiam.org/news/iam-local-62a.text: IAM Local 62A has officially opened contract negotiations with Collins Aerospace in Cheshire, Conn., as IAM members prepare to bargain for a strong agreement that recognizes the skill, experience, and contributions of their workforce.; The Local 62A negotiating committee is entering bargaining united and prepared, with committee members recently completing contract negotiation preparation training at the IAM’s William W.; Now, the negotiating committee is focused on securing a contract that reflects the value of that work and addresses the priorities of the membership.; “As they enter these negotiations, they should know that their union stands firmly behind them.; They have earned a contract that recognizes their contributions, and the IAM Union will be there every step of the way as they fight for the wages, benefits, protections, and future they deserve.” As bargaining gets underway, the negotiating committee is focused on building a strong contract campaign, keeping members informed and engaged, and making sure the priorities of the workforce remain front and center at the bargaining table.; When a negotiating committee and its membership stand united, they send a powerful message that they are ready to fight for a contract that respects the value of their work.” The committee’s recent training at the Winpisinger Center provided hands-on preparation in bargaining strategy, contract campaign planning, legal issues, and member engagement.; “Preparation gives a negotiating committee the confidence and discipline to walk into the bargaining room ready for the challenges ahead,” said IAM Resident General Vice President Jody Bennett.; Now, they are ready to take that preparation to the table and make sure the voices of their fellow members are heard.” IAM District 26 leadership emphasized that the strength of the negotiations will ultimately depend on the involvement of the entire membership.; “Our job is to make sure those priorities are represented clearly and forcefully throughout negotiations.; The more engaged our membership is, the stronger position we have to secure an agreement that reflects what these members have earned.” Local 62A leadership also stressed that negotiations are about more than what happens inside the bargaining room.; “Every member has a role to play as we move through these negotiations,” said Local 62A President Noel Rodriguez.; This committee has prepared itself to clearly present the priorities of its membership and to negotiate with the determination and professionalism that IAM members bring to their jobs every day.” IAM District 26 Business Representative Dianna Koch emphasized the importance of ensuring the contract recognizes the skill and contributions of Local 62A members.; “The training provided at the Winpisinger Center gives our negotiating committee the tools, confidence, and strategic preparation needed to advocate effectively for our members.; We are committed to securing an agreement that delivers meaningful improvements and protects the interests of the workforce for years to come.” With contract negotiations now underway, IAM Local 62A members are standing together and ready to fight for a strong agreement that recognizes their contributions, protects their future, and rewards the skilled work they perform every day.

https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/ge-heal.title: GE HealthCare Accused of Bad-Faith Bargaining as IAM Union Seeks Congressional Intervention
https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/ge-heal.text: denying annual raises and delaying a first contract to workers AURORA, Ohio, July 30, 2026 – The 600,000-member IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers) is calling on Ohio’s congressional delegation to intervene as GE HealthCare continues to delay a first contract for approximately 130 IAM-represented workers at its Aurora, Ohio manufacturing facility after more than 18 months of contentious negotiations and repeated alleged violations of federal labor law.; The outreach comes as Congress considers the Faster Labor Contracts Act , legislation designed to impose stricter penalties on employers that refuse to negotiate first contracts in good faith.; The charges include allegations that the company canceled bargaining sessions, made regressive proposals, and unlawfully refused to maintain the status quo by withholding previously scheduled wage increases after workers chose union representation.; We care about the quality of our work because we know it makes a real difference in people’s lives,” said Montana Hayes, a Production Associate at GE HealthCare and member of the IAM Local 1363 Negotiations Committee.; After more than 18 months, it’s time for the company to stop delaying and negotiate the fair first contract we’ve earned.” The company’s proposal cuts wages below employees’ current pay rates, slashes paid time off, and increases healthcare costs for workers and their families.; “GE HealthCare has chosen to drag out negotiations instead of respecting its employees’ decision to form a union and negotiate a fair first contract,” said IAM Eastern Territory General Vice President David Sullivan.; They deserve a company that negotiates in good faith—not delay tactics, regressive proposals and unlawful conduct.; We will continue standing shoulder to shoulder with Local 1363 until GE HealthCare does the right thing and these workers secure the contract they’ve earned.” The approximately 130 IAM Local 1363 members at GE HealthCare’s Aurora facility voted to join the IAM Union in January 2025 and have been negotiating their first collective bargaining agreement ever since.

https://www.goiam.org/news/iam-union-tha.text: WASHINGTON, July 22, 2026 — The IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers), which represents more than 100,000 workers across the airline and railroad industries, is thanking former National Mediation Board (NMB) Member Deirdre Hamilton for her service following her dismissal by the Trump Administration, a move made possible by a recent Supreme Court decision allowing the arbitrary removal of officials serving on independent federal labor boards.; Hamilton, a respected labor attorney and former IAM Legal Fellow, brought decades of labor law experience to the National Mediation Board, the independent federal agency responsible for administering the Railway Labor Act and helping resolve labor-management disputes in the rail and airline industries.; “Deirdre Hamilton has dedicated her career to standing up for working people, and her service on the National Mediation Board reflected that commitment every day,” said IAM Union International President Brian Bryant .; “As a former IAM Legal Fellow, Deirdre understands the challenges facing workers and the critical role the NMB plays in ensuring fair labor relations across the rail and airline industries.; “Independent agencies like the National Mediation Board exist to provide stability, fairness and confidence in the collective bargaining process.; Their independence is essential to ensuring workers and employers alike receive fair treatment under the law.” Before joining the NMB, Hamilton built a distinguished career in labor law and labor relations, including serving as an IAM Legal Fellow early in her career.

https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/iam-uni.text: House of Representatives passed the bipartisan Faster Labor Contracts Act (FLCA), legislation designed to stop employers from delaying negotiations and denying newly organized workers the first contract they fought to win.; Employers would be required to begin negotiations within 10 days of workers voting to form a union.; If no agreement is reached within 90 days, the parties can move to mediation, followed by binding arbitration if necessary.; Workers currently wait an average of more than 458 days to secure a first contract, according to a Bloomberg analysis, often because employers intentionally stall negotiations after losing a union election.; “Workers don’t organize a union just to spend years waiting for their employer to negotiate a contract,” said Bryant.

https://www.goiam.org/news/imail/iam-uni.text: Approximately 5,000 members of IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers) District 776 in Fort Worth, Texas, voted on Sunday to ratify a new contract with the largest defense contractor in the U.S., Lockheed Martin.; The new contract includes: – Historic General Wage Increases (GWI increases 6.0%, 4.5%, 4.5%, 4.0%, 4.0%) – Improve/Maintain Quality of Life: No Mandatory Overtime and Increased Vacation – Improvements to Retirement – $6,000 Ratification Bonus and more .; IAM Union District 776’s negotiating committee unanimously recommended the proposal, which the members voted to accept.; Contract negotiations have been ongoing since mid-March of this year.; “Keeping with their mission-critical mantra, the members fought hard for a worthy contract, and they prevailed – the entire IAM is proud of their commitment.” Negotiations are crucial for IAM District 776 members and their families, as well as for the Dallas-Fort Worth community.; READ: 2027 Defense Authorization Appropriation Bill – Support for the F-35 Program “Our members made it clear what the purpose and goal for these negotiations were,” said District 776 Directing Business Representative Doyle Huddleston .; We did what our members asked us to do, and they made the decision with their votes.” The IAM District 776 negotiating team participated in an extensive preparation course held at their district offices in January.; This instrumental coursework covers drafting contract language, strategic planning, contract costing, communications, and negotiation simulation.; “From the preparation preceding these negotiations to sitting down in each committee to center the right energies, the negotiation team presented and defended the desires of their members,” said IAM Southern Territory General Vice President Craig Martin .; Today, the membership agreed that the negotiations addressed their concerns.; The negotiating committee took those wishes to heart and worked to bring a solid proposal to the membership for consideration.

“The training Local 62A received will help ensure they enter negotiations united, prepared, and ready to advocate for every member they represent.” The program also emphasized contract organizing techniques designed to keep members informed, engaged, and mobilized throughout the bargaining process.; A strong, active membership remains one of the most powerful tools available to any negotiating committee.; “The members of this negotiating committee have demonstrated their commitment to their coworkers by taking the time to sharpen their skills and strengthen their strategy.; That dedication will serve them well when they sit down across the table from management.” “Armed with new knowledge, practical experience, and a clear vision for their bargaining objectives, the IAM Local 62A negotiating committee is preparing to enter negotiations with professionalism, determination, and the full support of the IAM Union behind them,” said IAM Aerospace Coordinator Stephen Jordan.; https://afacwa.org/united-flight-attenda.text: During our final Mediated Session this week in Washington, D.C., we reached a Tentative Agreement based on the priorities you identified in these targeted negotiations.; Some of the changes achieved in Tentative Agreement Two (TA2) include: Improved Base Pay Rates Restrictions on red-eye flying Sit Pay for scheduled and rescheduled sits over 2.5 hours Increased money for Retro payments Improved language in Hotels and Electronic Notification The Tentative Agreement will be presented to AFA United Master Executive Council (MEC) at a Special Meeting on Wednesday, April 1st.; The MEC, which is comprised of the 14 Local Presidents, will review and vote on whether to send the Tentative Agreement for Membership Ratification.; If approved by the MEC, we will release full details of the Tentative Agreement on Friday, April 3rd.; During the ratification process, Members will receive access to the following: Full Tentative Agreement language (PDF Full Text) Summary of Changes Pay Calculators Informational articles, videos, and graphics In addition to the online support at UnitedFAcontract.org , Members will also receive a printed copy of the Summary & Voting Booklet, along with their confidential voting credentials, mailed to the address on file.; Voting on the Tentative Agreement will open on April 23rd at noon ET and close on May 12th at noon ET.; If the Tentative Agreement is ratified by the Membership, the improved pay scales and Boarding Pay would go into effect on May 31, with the June Bid period.; In Solidarity, Your Negotiating Committee, Ken Diaz, MEC President Melinda Beal, Chairperson Chris Bruton, Council 9 President Randy Hatfield, Council 22 President Important Dates: APR 1-2 – MEC TA2 Review APR 3 – TA2 Materials Available to Members APR 7 – Virtual Roadshows Start APR 13 – Summary & Voting Booklets in Mail APR 23 – Voting Opens Noon ET MAY 12 – Voting Closes Noon ET

https://afacwa.org/correcting-united-man.title: Correcting United Management Negotiations Propaganda
https://afacwa.org/correcting-united-man.text: At the end of United management’s February 27, 2026 company propaganda email on negotiations they included this outrageous lie and distortion of profit sharing value.; AFA leadership previously stated that its negotiation strategy was to wait for other carriers to complete agreements before finalizing one at United.; In fact, AFA loaned their Chief Negotiator to American to help with their negotiations.; After American reached its agreement, AFA replaced its United negotiating committee, brought back its Chief Negotiator and resumed negotiations at United.; Here’s the truth: The February 27th negotiations “update” from the United’s Labor Relations presents their position on the content of the contract and that will be handled at the negotiating table this week.; We have communicated what we are fighting for and we will continue to keep you closely informed as we press for a tentative agreement that you can ratify.; The task of negotiating TA2 within the remaining March sessions, or even within this week for that matter, is entirely doable.; Setting the Record Straight – The end of their “update” offers a wild story about AFA wanting to wait for other airlines to negotiate before reaching an agreement with United.; There is no reason that AFA would ever want to delay negotiations since in regular negotiations.; Every chance to move negotiations forward was blocked by management.; When negotiations started the United AFA Negotiating Committee requested the assistance of a specific AFA attorney, not the Director of Collective Bargaining.; Only after this decision not to use our most experienced negotiator did we approve loaning our Director of Collective Bargaining to assist with the negotiations between APFA and American.; (To be clear, APFA paid for the assistance of our negotiator).; On September 6, 2023, the United Master Executive Council unanimously adopted a resolution to approach management about expediting negotiations to reach agreement in “months, not years.” Even though management had previously suggested an expedited process, when the MEC President approached them with a proposal they took months to review it and ultimately refused.; While American and Alaska were able to use a credible threat of a release to force agreements in those negotiations, United management delayed talks beyond the U.S.; In the fall of 2024, the United MEC President invited our General Counsel and Director of Collective Bargaining to the negotiations in order to make an assessment of the time it would take to negotiate over the remaining proposals and helped the MEC (all elected Local Council Presidents) review the status of negotiations.; It was decided that negotiations should take a different approach in order to move the process forward.; The members of the Negotiating Committee were changed and the new approach was implemented, amping up pressure on management, gaining support from lawmakers , and making it possible to conclude the remaining 80% of negotiations within four months.

https://atd142.org/iam-district-142-to-a.title: IAM District 142 to Alaska Management: Get Serious!
https://atd142.org/iam-district-142-to-a.text: Dear Sisters and Brothers: The IAM District 142 Alaska-Hawaiian Negotiating Committee and Alaska Airlines management met this week and continued joint contract negotiations for almost 8,000 Alaska-Hawaiian ground workers.; Since the announcement of the Alaska-Hawaiian merger, your Negotiating Committee has been very clear with the Company that the protection of our work from outsourcing without a drop-dead date, the safeguarding of our jobs from the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI), and the opportunity for IAM members to grow with the Company via insourcing future work is of utmost importance.; We urge ALL IAM members at Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines to stay informed and educated regarding these contract negotiations.; Sincerely and fraternally, Jesse Wilson General Chair David Figueira General Chair Joint Negotiating Committee: Alaska COPS : Melissa Hopson, Jane McGrath, Andrea Mondoy-Honaker, Sandra Hagan Alaska RSSA : Mark Walker, Garrett Gebauer Hawaiian COSFP : Mana Kanahele, Ku’ulei McGuire, Phyllis Moleta-Torres VIEW/DOWNLOAD A PDF VERSION OF THIS BULLETIN POST ON ALL IAM BULLETIN BOARDS

https://atd142.org/iam-qantas-airways-la.title: IAM/Qantas Airways LAX Mediation Update
https://atd142.org/iam-qantas-airways-la.text: Dear Sisters and Brothers: Following the announcement of the IAM Union, Air Transport District 142 filing for mediation under the auspices of the National Mediation Board (NMB) on 7/23/26, we wanted to give you more information about where we are in that process.; We are extremely pleased that the NMB received and processed our application in a very timely manner.; We have been assigned to NMB Mediator Michael Donatelli.; Donatelli spent his career being active within his ALPA bargaining unit in various capacities and brings with him a wealth of airline operational and negotiation experience at both the ALPA local and international level.; It is of primary importance for everyone to understand that the NMB and their mediators control when, where, and how long Unions and Companies meet; in mediation.; We are aware that the NMB is requiring the parties to meet in the home cities of the mediators.; Your District 142 and International Representatives have had an initial call with Mediator Donatelli and have proffered dates for him to consider for our next meetings.; If you would like to know more about negotiations under the Railway Labor Act (RLA) and the NMB’s role, please visit the link below or simply Google “mediation under the RLA”.; https://nmb.gov/NMB_Application/index.php/meditation-overview-faq We are still planning a membership engagement away from the airport and Qantas facilities where you can come and meet your negotiators and get answers to any questions you may have.; Go to our website at https://atd142.org and click the buttons at the top of the homepage to “Join Our Email List” and “Sign Up for Text Messages.” It takes less than five minutes to sign up for both, and you will be assured of receiving timely updates whenever there is news regarding your contract negotiations.

https://atd142.org/qantas-negotiations-u.title: QANTAS NEGOTIATIONS UPDATE – IAM UNION FILES FOR MEDIATION
https://atd142.org/qantas-negotiations-u.text: Dear Sisters and Brothers: As a follow-up to last week’s meetings held at the QF facility in LAX, your negotiations committee wants to bring you up to date on the most recent developments that have occurred as a result of negotiations.; At the meetings that occurred in PHX in June, and as was communicated to you then, your committee put forward a comprehensive proposal with very specific discussions and associated requirements to close these negotiations.; It is important to note that we are not speaking about dollars and cents as those can still be negotiated.; Under the Railway Labor Act (RLA), this would be referred to as an impasse in direct negotiations which qualifies to trigger the next step.; The next step would be to enlist the services of the National Mediation Board (NMB).; The Union communicated its intent to file for mediation to the Company within the last 24 hours and this bulletin signifies the application has been submitted to the NMB.; While invoking mediation will lengthen negotiations, it will also ensure that the Company has to follow certain conventions that occur in negotiations.; The net result of that will be the achievement of the best CBA possible for your ratification consideration.; Go to our website at https://atd142.org and click the buttons at the top of the homepage to “Join Our Email List” and “Sign Up for Text Messages.” It takes less than five minutes to sign up for both, and you will be ensured of receiving timely updates whenever there is news regarding your contract negotiations.

https://atd142.org/twu-iam-association-m.text: July 3, 2026 TWU/IAM Association M&R Membership Bulletin Negotiations Committees Meet to Prepare for Upcoming Bargaining Brothers and Sisters, The TWU/IAM Association Negotiating Committee met this week in Phoenix, Arizona, with the negotiations subcommittees representing our Maintenance & Related (M&R), Maintenance Control Technicians (MCT), Maintenance Training Specialists (MTS), and Material Logistics Specialists (MLS), Maintenance and Logistics Planners, Quality Assurance Auditors, and Technical Document Specialists work groups to begin preparations for upcoming negotiations with American Airlines, which are scheduled to begin on April 1, 2027.; These meetings focused on identifying the contractual priorities, many from the prior round of contract negotiations preparations, and also identified newer concerns that matter most to our members.; Although each work group faces distinct challenges, we remain united in our goal: to negotiate the strongest contracts that recognize the professionalism, skill, and dedication of every TWU/IAM Association member and sets a new industry standard for wages and benefits.; These surveys will give every member the opportunity to identify their bargaining priorities, share existing contractual concerns, and help the negotiation committee shape the proposals presented at the bargaining table.; Your feedback will play a critical role in ensuring that our negotiating agenda reflects the priorities of the entire membership.; Your voice matters, and every response strengthens our ability to negotiate from a position of unity.; With early openers for negotiations set to begin on April 1, 2027, the TWU/IAM Association remains committed to keeping the membership informed through regular updates.; We encourage you to stay engaged, support your Negotiating Committee, encourage your fellow members to participate, and continue demonstrating the solidarity that has always been the foundation of our strength.; In Solidarity, The TWU/IAM Association Negotiating Committee VIEW/PRINT A PDF VERSION OF THIS BULLETIN POST ON ALL ASSOCIATION BULLETIN BOARDS

https://atd142.org/lufthansa-technik-wor.text: Haga clic aquí para la versión en español Lufthansa Technik workers in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, have ratified their first Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with the IAM District 142, securing job protections, a signing bonus, wage increases, and improved benefits.; The agreement, covering more than 200 aircraft mechanics and related workers, follows nearly four years of negotiations driven by strong member advocacy and solidarity.; Throughout negotiations, IAM Union leadership worked closely with the bargaining committee and membership to ensure workers’ voices remained front and center and to push the process forward despite delays.; “This agreement shows what we can accomplish when we stay united,” said the IAM Lufthansa Technik Negotiating Committee.; Since then, negotiations have been marked by delays, prompting the IAM to seek federal mediation in 2023 and rally support locally and internationally.; In December 2025, workers overwhelmingly rejected a decertification effort backed by anti-union forces, reaffirming their commitment to the IAM and sending a clear message that they were united in their fight for a fair contract.

https://www.amfanational.org/?zone=/unio.title: AMFA-SWA AMT Negotiations Update #1
https://www.amfanational.org/?zone=/unio.text: AMFA-SWA AMT Negotiations Update #1 Aug 24, 2026 August 24, 2026 Participants for AMFA: Bret Oestreich – National President Earl Clark – Region I Director Wilber "Will" Abbott – Region II Director Louis Upchurch – Local 4 ALR Frank Suentzenich – Local 11 ALR Wayne Lampley – Local 18 ALR Ken Patrick – Local 32 ALR Lucas Middlebrook – Legal Counsel Peter Manikowski – Economist Participants for Southwest Airlines: Michelle Jordan - Mng.; Ops Production Rob Jones – Senior Lead Counsel/Chief Negotiator Kris Townsend – Sr.; Mng., Labor Planning/Analytics Kevin Chen – Labor Planning/Analytics The AMFA-Southwest Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) Negotiating Committee (the “Committee”) is providing this update to the Membership at Southwest Airlines (“Southwest”).; This is the Committee's only official source of negotiating communications.; The Committee held a four-day collective bargaining session (August 18-21) with Southwest Airlines in Denver, Co.; In support of this exercise, the parties negotiated and entered into a Protocol Agreement setting parameters for these off-the-record exploratory discussions.; Once terminated, the parties would proceed away from extension discussions and into a more comprehensive negotiation process.; The Protocol Agreement also ensures that once either side terminates the agreement, everything discussed during the exploratory phase will be without prejudice to and not affect any future negotiation position.; We would like to thank all the observers that took time from their days to attend and experience the negotiation process.; In addition, we would like to express our gratitude to the many members that reached out to provide their support during this first week of negotiation.; Fraternally, AMFA-SWA AMT Negotiating Committee Search Site Map RSS Feeds - AMFA 7853 E.

https://cwa-union.org/news/releases/acti.title: Activision Quality Assurance Workers Vote to Authorize Strike
https://cwa-union.org/news/releases/acti.text: Activision Quality Assurance Workers Vote to Authorize Strike October 15, 2026 Ahead of next week’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 early access launch, workers at Microsoft-owned Activision Publishing vote to strike if necessary to achieve a fair union contract NATIONWIDE — On Thursday, October 15, quality assurance testers at Activision Publishing—represented by Communications Workers of America (CWA) Locals 6215, 7250, and 9400—have overwhelmingly voted to authorize a strike following recent delays at the bargaining table, giving CWA President Claude Cummings Jr.; the authority to call for a strike if negotiations continue to stall.; Activision Quality Assurance United-CWA (AQAU-CWA) and Activision have been negotiating for a first contract for over two years.; The breakdown in negotiations caused by the company’s delays comes at a critical time in the production and release cycle of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, one of Activision’s most profitable franchises.; Shortly after forming a union, members of AQAU-CWA’s bargaining committee engaged in contract negotiations with Activision Publishing in August 2024.; “Our members are tired of the stalling and are prepared to do what needs to be done to secure a fair contract, a fair wage, and fair working conditions for everyone.” “For two years, Activision Publishing has delayed and stalled negotiations rather than doing their duty to bargain in good faith with the dedicated workers who work on profit-shattering titles that the gaming community enjoys dearly,” said CWA District 7 Vice President Susie McAllister.; “The results of the strike authorization vote send a clear message to Activision management: it is time to stop playing games because our members are united and prepared to do what it takes to win the strong contract they deserve.” ### The Campaign to Organize Digital Employees (CODE-CWA) is a network of worker-organizers and their staff working every single day to build the voice and power necessary to ensure the future of the tech, game, and digital industries in the United States and Canada.

https://atd142.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: 100 Phoenix, Arizona 85044 (816) 982-6480 iamdl142@iamdl142.org https://atd142.org Date: July 30, 2026 File: QF – 2026 2026 – 145 IAM/Qantas Airways LAX Mediation Update Dear Sisters and Brothers: Following the announcement of the IAM Union, Air Transport District 142 filing for mediation under the auspices of the National Mediation Board (NMB) on 7/23/26, we wanted to give you more information about where we are in that process.; We are extremely pleased that the NMB received and processed our application in a very timely manner.; We have been assigned to NMB Mediator Michael Donatelli.; Donatelli spent his career being active within his ALPA bargaining unit in various capacities and brings with him a wealth of airline operational and negotiation experience at both the ALPA local and international level.; It is of primary importance for everyone to understand that the NMB and their mediators control when, where, and how long Unions and Companies meet; in mediation.; We are aware that the NMB is requiring the parties to meet in the home cities of the mediators.; Your District 142 and International Representatives have had an initial call with Mediator Donatelli and have proffered dates for him to consider for our next meetings.; If you would like to know more about negotiations under the Railway Labor Act (RLA) and the NMB’s role, please visit the link below or simply Google “mediation under the RLA”.; https://nmb.gov/NMB_Application/index.php/meditation-overview-faq/ We are still planning a membership engagement away from the airport and Qantas facilities where you can come and meet your negotiators and get answers to any questions you may have.; Go to our website at https://atd142.org and click the buttons at the top of the homepage to “Join Our Email List” and “Sign Up for Text Messages.” It takes less than five minutes to sign up for both, and you will be assured of receiving timely updates whenever there is news regarding your contract negotiations.

https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.title: April 21 UGE Negotiations Update
https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: United Ground Express (UGE) Contract Negotiations Update April 21, 2026 Dear Sisters and Brothers of United Ground Express (UGE), Following our last communication, we have decided to file for assistance with the National Mediation Board (NMB).; The NMB will now assign a neutral mediator to oversee our negotiations.; This mediator will work with both sides to facilitate communication and bridge gaps.; Please be aware that this process can take weeks or months, and the NMB will now determine the timing and location of all future meetings.; There are two primary outcomes to mediation: Both parties reach a tentative agreement for the members to vote on.; Or, if mediation fails, the NMB may offer binding arbitration.; If either side refuses arbitration, a 30- day "cooling off" period begins, after which a strike or lockout becomes legally permissible.; For this reason, RLA-covered contract negotiations are often slower than similar talks in other industries.; We must be prepared to show our collective strength, whether through verbal expression or informational picketing, to let the company and the flying public know that we deserve a contract comparable to other vendors in the industry.; In Solidarity , IAM District 141 Negotiating Team Warren Glenn Robert Jesel Chris Lusk John Staton, Jr.

https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: (847) 640-2222 @) IAM141.org United Airlines Negotiations Update 09 January 2026 Yesterday, an IAD Supervisor falsely told Union Members that the IAM rejected a company-offered $15 per hour Move Team premium to avoid upsetting Ramp Leads.; It appears the Company is attempting to negotiate in public and cannot - or will not - control supervisors who are actively spreading false information.; United should not allow officials to lie directly to employees about critical negotiation matters.; We hope to enter this final stage of negotiations soon.; Andrews is now authorized to speak on behalf of United Airlines regarding negotiations, we look forward to reviewing a formal written proposal from him concerning the premium increase he mentioned.; In Solidarity, IAM District 141 Negotiating Team Olu Ajetomobi Joe Bartz Jill Hazamy Victor Hernandez Barb Martin Terry Stansbury Faysal Silwany Erik Stenberg Sue Weisner Michael G.

https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.title: UA Negotiation Update 23 December 2025
https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: (847) 640-2222 @) IAM141.org United Airlines Negotiations Update 23 December 2025 Our negotiating team and United Airlines management continued discussions for our seven collective bargaining agreements in Chicago this past week.; Maintenance Instructor Contract Update Negotiations focused on Articles One, Four, Eight, and Eleven.; We made significant progress and completed several Tentative Agreements (TAs) related to: - 10-Hour Day and associated overtime - Union Hours - International Travel and Pay before Scheduled International Departure We have now completed all Non-Financial issues for this contract.; Although no tentative agreements were reached, we had very constructive and positive discussions regarding job preferencing and the triggers for bringing Storekeepers into a station where we are not currently performing work, as outlined in Article One of the agreement.; Passenger Service and Fleet Service Contract Update Negotiations continued to center on overtime, specifically the Company’s use of mandatory overtime.; We are happy to inform you that we have reached a tentative agreement that improves protection for our members when mandatory overtime is required and holds management more accountable when declaring it.; We are scheduled to continue negotiations the week of January 12, 2026, when the Fleet Technical Instructors subcommittee will join us.; On behalf of myself, the entire Negotiating Team, and all the Officers of District Lodge 141, we wish you and your families a very happy and healthy holiday season.; In solidarity, IAM District 141 Negotiating Team Olu Ajetomobi Joe Bartz Jill Hazamy Victor Hernandez Barb Martin Terry Stansbury Faysal Silwany Erik Stenberg Sue Weisner Michael G.

https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.title: UGE Negotiations Update 25 November 2025
https://iam141.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: (847) 640-2222 @) IAM141.org United Ground Express Negotiations Update 25 Novem ber 2025 Dear United Ground Express Members, As we noted last month, the final non-economic issue we needed to address was the "Wheels Up / Mandatory Overtime" situation.; We believe we have reached an agreement that will incentivize better shift scheduling, protecting the personal time of union members.; In addition, we are putting forward proposals that will improve paid holidays, increase Lead premiums, 401k matching, and a ratification bonus based on years of service, among other upgrades.; We are now awaiting UGE's response before setting the next negotiation session.; In Solidarity, IAM District 141 Negotiating Team Warren Glenn Robert Jesel Chris Lusk John Staton Jr.

https://atd142.org/wp-content/uploads/20.text: 100 Phoenix, Arizona 85044 (816) 982-6480 iamdl142@iamdl142.org https://atd142.org Date: May 5, 2026 File: LHT – 2026 2026 – 88 Lufthansa Technik Workers in Puerto Rico Ratify Strong First Contract Dear Sisters and Brothers: Lufthansa Technik workers in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, have ratified their first Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with the IAM District 142, securing job protections, a signing bonus, wage increases, and improved benefits.; The agreement, covering more than 200 aircraft mechanics and related workers, follows nearly four years of negotiations driven by strong member advocacy and solidarity.; Throughout negotiations, IAM Union leadership worked closely with the bargaining committee and membership to ensure workers’ voices remained front and center and to push the process forward despite delays.; “This agreement shows what we can accomplish when we stay united,” said the IAM Lufthansa Technik Negotiating Committee.; Since then, negotiations have been marked by delays, prompting the IAM to seek federal mediation in 2023 and rally support locally and internationally.; In December 2025, workers overwhelmingly rejected a decertification effort backed by anti-union forces, reaffirming their commitment to the IAM and sending a clear message that they were united in their fight for a fair contract.

https://www.goiam.org/news/arizona-iam-m.text: 25, 2026 — IAM Union (International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers) Local 933 members have ratified a new five-year contract with Raytheon in Tucson, securing significant wage increases, stronger benefits and expanded opportunities for career advancement.; A $3,000 ratification bonus , plus a $1,500 ratification 401(k) match.; These gains are an investment in the workers, their families and the community that depends on these good jobs.” Negotiations opened Oct.; 6 , following bargaining preparation that included member surveys, town halls, information sessions and training for the negotiating committee.; Members also held multiple solidarity rallies for a fair contract.; “This is a historic and unprecedented contract at Raytheon that gives our members more to count on, from their next paycheck to the years ahead,” said IAM Western Territory International Representative and Chief Negotiator Paul Shepherd.; “The negotiating committee worked hard to reach an agreement that recognizes their experience and supports a strong future here in Tucson and shares in the profits and success of the important work they do.; They earned it, and they had the final say.” The IAM negotiating committee included Raytheon workers and IAM members Wendel Jackson, Abe Alapizco, Abe Gutierrez, Stefeny Gutierrez, Gerard Klovos, Lee Suzuki and Junior Alegria.“I want to thank our negotiating committee for staying focused on the membership through some tough conversations at the table,” continued Martinez.; “Our members backed them up every step of the way, and that made a difference in bringing this contract home.” The negotiating team also received support from the IAM International Union and the IAM Western Territory.; IAM Local 933 Negotiating Committee

https://www.goiam.org/news/iam-journal/l.title: Local S6 Members Secure Historic Agreement at Bath Iron Works
https://www.goiam.org/news/iam-journal/l.text: Following months of preparation, member engagement and determined bargaining, approximately 4,500 IAM Local S6 members voted overwhelmingly to ratify a new collective bargaining agreement with Bath Iron Works, a subsidiary of General Dynamics.; A Membership-Driven Contract Long before formal negotiations began, Local S6’s bargaining committee was already hard at work.; Shop-floor conversations, member meetings and direct feedback helped shape every proposal presented during negotiations.; Rather than entering negotiations with predetermined objectives, the committee focused on representing the concerns voiced by the membership.; “When a ship leaves this yard, you know a part of your work will protect our nation’s sailors for decades to come,” said Negotiating Committee Member Tim Halle.; That’s how we keep this shipyard, and our union strong for years to come.” Eastern Territory staff led by GVP Sullivan, Chief of Staff Lorie Wilson, and Territory Coordinator George Edwards meet with the Local S6 Negotiating and Strike Committees to discuss strategy and plans of action.; Months before formal negotiations began, committee members reviewed proposals, analyzed economic trends, prepared bargaining strategies, and worked through potential scenarios.; That work allowed negotiators to remain focused throughout the process and respond quickly as discussions evolved.; Throughout negotiations, members remained engaged, informed, and supportive of the committee representing them.; The agreement ultimately reflected not only months of negotiations,; “Every member has a voice,” said IAM Local S6 Communicator, Shop Steward, Joint Apprenticeship, and Negotiating Committees Member Devin Ragnar.; I congratulate the negotiating committee and every Local S6 member who stood together to secure a stronger future for themselves and their families.” For Local S6, the story has never been solely about ships.

https://cwa-union.org/news/cwaers-fight-.title: CWAers Fight Back With Powerful Pickets
https://cwa-union.org/news/cwaers-fight-.text: CWAers Fight Back With Powerful Pickets October 22, 2026 AT&T Forged Fiber On October 20, Fiber Technicians and Facility Specialists at Forged Fiber, AT&T’s newest wholesale fiber joint venture, launched informational pickets across eight states (Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Iowa, Minnesota, Oregon, Utah, and Washington) to demand a fair contract.; At stake in negotiations is AT&T’s attempt to outsource critical infrastructure work to non-union contractors, despite directly employing over 1,100 highly-trained union technicians who transferred from Lumen Technologies when AT&T acquired its fiber business earlier this year.; These pickets come just as AT&T is seeking regulatory approval to sell a 50% stake in Forged Fiber to BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.; Our members at Forged Fiber are demanding that AT&T bargain in good faith and not put our communities and customers at risk by using substandard contracted services.” ~~~ Seattle Times In September, approximately 60 CWA members at the Seattle Times—represented by the Pacific Northwest Newspaper Guild (TNG-CWA Local 37082)—engaged in their first informational picket in over 20 years in response to months of delays at the bargaining table.; After more than six months of negotiating, members and management are no closer to agreement on wage increases.; ~~~ Horizon Air AFA-CWA Flight Attendants with Horizon Air, along with allies, were out in force last week, picketing for a living-wage contract at six airports across the western United States, including Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (pictured above) .; Click here to watch a recap of the Horizon Air pickets .

https://cwa-union.org/news/releases/forg.title: Forged Fiber Technicians and Facility Specialists Launch Multi-State Picket Ahead of AT&T’s 50% Sale of Network to BlackRock and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board
https://cwa-union.org/news/releases/forg.text: Forged Fiber Technicians and Facility Specialists Launch Multi-State Picket Ahead of AT&T’s 50% Sale of Network to BlackRock and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board October 19, 2026 NATIONWIDE – On Tuesday, Fiber Technicians and Facility Specialists at Forged Fiber, AT&T’s newest wholesale fiber joint venture, will launch informational pickets across nine states (Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Iowa, Minnesota, Oregon, Utah, and Washington) to demand a fair contract.; At stake in negotiations is AT&T’s attempt to outsource critical infrastructure work to non-union contractors, despite directly employing over 1,100 of highly-trained unionized technicians who transferred from Lumen Technologies when AT&T acquired its fiber business earlier this year.; These pickets come just as AT&T is seeking regulatory approval to sell a 50% stake in Forged Fiber to BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.
